evals.name: sql-to-qualify-eval-1-sample-transcript
evals.prompt: Run sql-to-qualify on the sample transcript.
evals.expected_output: All five rubric dimensions scored Covered/Partial/Missed with cited evidence, closing with a single advance/disqualify/needs-one-more-touch read naming the deciding dimension(s).
expectations: Scores all five rubric dimensions with a Status of Covered, Partial, or Missed
Marks contact reachability as Covered or Partial since Marcus lacks budget authority but names Priya and Sarah as a path to the decision-maker
Marks pain restated in the prospect's own words as Covered, citing the Twitter escalation incident in Marcus's own language rather than the whitepaper download
Marks budget/urgency plausibility as Covered or Partial, citing the ~$40k prior QA tool spend and the Q4 peak-season deadline
Marks competitive awareness as Covered or Partial, citing that Gong was evaluated for a different use case and no support-monitoring vendor has been engaged yet
Marks concrete next meeting booked as Covered, citing the specific Thursday 2pm session with Marcus, Priya, and Sarah
Closes with a single advance / disqualify / needs one more touch read naming the deciding dimension(s)
Cites a direct quote or timestamp as evidence for each non-Unclear dimension

evals.name: sql-to-qualify-eval-2-crm-export-csv
evals.prompt: Run sql-to-qualify on a CRM export CSV of SQL-stage leads.
evals.expected_output: A structural hygiene sweep, not a call-quality audit: a table of lead name, days since SQL, stage, and dimensions missing, sorted by days since SQL descending, stating explicitly that this checks whether fields were filled in.
expectations: Treats the file as a structural hygiene sweep rather than a call-quality audit
Checks rows marked SQL or later for populated, non-trivial contact role, stated pain, budget/urgency signal, and next-meeting date fields
Outputs a table with lead name, days since SQL, stage, and dimensions missing, sorted by days since SQL descending
States explicitly that this checks whether fields were filled in, not whether the underlying call was good
